plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flower clusters (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. In frost-free regions it grows into a large landscape shrub several meters tall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; widely grown in warm climates such as California, Florida, the Mediterranean, and Australia, and as a potted plant worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias only develop their colorful bracts when nights are long, needing about 12 to 14 hours of uninterrupted darkness for several weeks, which is why they color up around the holidays.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often lightly fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and tolerates more sun.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated across the southeastern United States, the UK, Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are related to the tea plant, and their seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics in Japan and China.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low, clump-forming perennial with leathery evergreen leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens that age to pinkish green. It thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to mountain woodlands of the Alps and the northern Apennines in central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas rose is not a true rose but a buttercup relative, and all parts of it are toxic.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like feathery leaves that erupts in huge clusters of vivid blossoms. The flowers are followed by long, dark woody seed pods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere tropics (October to January in places such as Brazil and Australia); blooms in May to July in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Brazil, northern Australia, India, the Caribbean, and Africa
plants.funFact: The royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar even though it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees in the world.
